description: French decimal comma; integers carry no decimal part. Do NOT implement this with a locale-aware formatter — those add thousands separators and vary by platform and OS version. The rule is literally "stringify, then replace . with ,".

cases.why: The common case, and the one that shows the separator is a comma rather than the dot a default toString would produce.
An integer renders "2", not "2,0". A fixed-one-decimal formatter fails here.
Renders "0,5" and not ",5". Some locale formatters drop the leading zero for values below one, which is why this is pinned rather than assumed.
The value produced by the 80 g / 64 g portion tie, so the two suites join up here.
No thousands separator and no space; a locale formatter may insert one.
Zero counts as an integer, so it renders "0" and not "0,0". Reachable whenever an ingredient is scaled all the way down.
